overview.text: Mair's (Common) Keelback is a harmless water snake of northern and eastern Australia and New Guinea. It is one of the few Australian snakes that can eat small cane toads without being poisoned.

identification.text: Olive, brown or blackish with small black spots or crossbars; strongly ridged (keeled) scales. It looks like the venomous Rough-scaled Snake.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Northern and eastern Australia (Western Australia to New South Wales), southern Papua New Guinea and Indonesian New Guinea.

diet.text: Mainly frogs, plus small fish, lizards and mammals.

recognise.text: Keeled scales and dark spots, near fresh water.
